3086-original-short-stories-volume-10.title: Original Short Stories Volume 10
3086-original-short-stories-volume-10.creator: Guy De Maupassant
3086-original-short-stories-volume-10.description: A book by Guy De Maupassant. “Go into one of their huts; you will never find the father there. If you ask the woman what has become of her husband, she will stretch her arms out over the dark ocean which rumbles and roars along the coast. He remained, there one night, when he had had too much to drink; so did her oldest son. She has four more big, strong, fair-haired boys. Soon it will be their time.

50639-romany-life-experienced-and-observ.title: With The Gypsies
50639-romany-life-experienced-and-observ.creator: Frank Cuttriss
50639-romany-life-experienced-and-observ.description: A book by Frank Cuttriss. The terms “gypsy” and “tramp” are by many considered synonymous. It is not, however, by any means the case, for while gypsies may be, and sometimes are, mistaken for tramps, the genuine professional tramp and the Tachey Romany, or true gypsy, have very little in common.

67056-the-japanese-new-year-s-festival-g.description: A book by Helen C. Gunsaulus. nd mode of living of the people of Japan rather than of assembling together pictures which would be enjoyed for their aesthetic appeal. While these prints are of an artistic nature, they are valuable to an institution of this kind as approaches to the study of the ethnology of Japan.

arxiv-1311-3930.title: An adaptive finite element method for the infinity Laplacian
arxiv-1311-3930.creator: Omar Lakkis, Tristan Pryer
arxiv-1311-3930.description: Abstract We construct a finite element method (FEM) for the infinity Laplacian. Solutions of this problem are well known to be singular in nature so we have taken the opportunity to conduct an a posteriori analysis of the method deriving residual based estimators to drive an adaptive algorithm.

arxiv-2004-03082.title: egg : Fast and Extensible Equality Saturation
arxiv-2004-03082.creator: Max Willsey, Chandrakana Nandi, Yisu Remy Wang, Oliver Flatt, Zachary Tatlock, Pavel Panchekha
arxiv-2004-03082.description: Abstract . An e-graph efficiently represents a congruence relation over many expressions. Although they were originally developed in the late 1970s for use in automated theorem provers, a more recent technique known as equality saturation repurposes e-graphs to implement state-of-the-art, rewrite-driven compiler optimizations and program synthesizers. However, e-graphs remain unspecialized for this newer use case.

arxiv-2107-04276.title: Secure Consensus via Objective Coding: Robustness Analysis to Channel Tampering
arxiv-2107-04276.creator: Marco Fabris, Daniel Zelazo
arxiv-2107-04276.description: Abstract This work mainly addresses continuous-time multiagent consensus networks where an adverse attacker affects the convergence performances of said protocol. In particular, we develop a novel secure-by-design approach in which the presence of a network manager monitors the system and broadcasts encrypted tasks (i.e., hidden edge weight assignments) to the agents involved.

arxiv-2207-10458.title: Remodelling of the fibre-aggregate structure of collagen gels by cancer-associated fibroblasts: a time-resolved grey-tone image analysis based on stochastic modelling
arxiv-2207-10458.creator: Cedric J. Gommes 1, Thomas Louis 2, Isabelle Bourgot 2, Erik Maquoi 2, Silvia Blacher 2, Agnès Noël 2
arxiv-2207-10458.description: Abstract Solid tumors consist of tumor cells associated with stromal and immune cells, secreted factors and extracellular matrix (ECM), that together constitute the tumor microenvironment. Among stromal cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are of particular interest. CAFs modulate the architecture of the ECM by exerting forces and contracting collagen fibres, creating paths that facilitate cancer cell migration.

arxiv-2212-08273.title: Learning for Vehicle-to-Vehicle Cooperative Perception under Lossy Communication
arxiv-2212-08273.creator: Jinlong Li, Runsheng Xu, Xinyu Liu, Jin Ma, Zicheng Chi, Jiaqi Ma, Hongkai Yu
arxiv-2212-08273.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jinlong Li, Runsheng Xu, Xinyu Liu, Jin Ma, Zicheng Chi, Jiaqi Ma, Hongkai Yu. Deep learning has been widely used in intelligent vehicle driving perception systems, such as 3D object detection. One promising technique is Cooperative Perception, which leverages Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication to share deep learning-based features among vehicles. However, most cooperative perception algorithms assume ideal communication and do not consider the impact of Lossy Communication (LC), which is very common in the real world, on feature sharing.

arxiv-2304-10427.title: On the Potential of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Data Exploration of Federated Bioinformatics Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2304-10427.creator: Ana Claudia Sima, Tarcisio Mendes de Farias
arxiv-2304-10427.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ana Claudia Sima, Tarcisio Mendes de Farias. In this paper, we present work in progress on the role of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots, such as ChatGPT, in facilitating data access to federated knowledge graphs. In particular, we provide examples from the field of bioinformatics, to illustrate the potential use of Conversational AI to describe datasets, as well as generate and explain (federated) queries across datasets for the benefit of domain experts.

arxiv-2402-07952.title: On the inverse Möbius transformation and unrestricted partitions
arxiv-2402-07952.creator: Romulo L. Cruz-Simbron
arxiv-2402-07952.description: Abstract . In this work we explore the relationship between the Möbius inverse transformation of an arbitrary sequence and unrestricted partitions identities. 1. Introduction A partition of a number n is a sequence denoted by \pi=(k_{1},k_{2},\cdots) comprising non-negative integers, with a finite subset of the k_{i} being nonzero.

arxiv-2510-11821.title: H H -harmonic reproducing kernels on the ball
arxiv-2510-11821.creator: Matěj Moravík
arxiv-2510-11821.description: Abstract We consider the Szegő reproducing kernel associated with the space of H H -harmonic functions on the unit ball in n-dimensional space, i.e. functions that are characterized by being annihilated by the hyperbolic Laplacian. This paper derives an explicit series expansion for the reproducing kernel in terms of a triple hypergeometric function introduced of Exton.

arxiv-2511-16087.title: AssayMatch: Learning to Select Data for Molecular Activity Models
arxiv-2511-16087.creator: Vincent Fan, Regina Barzilay
arxiv-2511-16087.description: Abstract The performance of machine learning models in drug discovery is highly dependent on the quality and consistency of the underlying training data. Due to limitations in dataset sizes, many models are trained by aggregating bioactivity data from diverse sources, including public databases such as ChEMBL. However, this approach often introduces significant noise due to variability in experimental protocols.

plos-pone-0009404.creator: Anna Torri, Ottavio Beretta, Anna Ranghetti et al.
plos-pone-0009404.description: PLOS ONE research article. Dendritic cells (DCs) constitute a heterogeneous group of antigen-presenting leukocytes important in activation of both innate and adaptive immunity. We studied the gene expression patterns of DCs incubated with reagents inducing their activation or inhibition. Total RNA was isol

pmc-10556168.title: Introduction: Indology and Aryanism: Knowledge of India in Nazi Germany—An Invitation for New Research
pmc-10556168.creator: Moritz Epple, Maria Framke, Eli Franco, Horst Junginger, Baijayanti Roy
pmc-10556168.description: The introduction to our special issue offers a brief survey of the historical literature on knowledge about India in Nazi Germany and distinguishes three different, but interrelated layers of such knowledge: disciplinary knowledge of Indology as an academic field, knowledge fulfilling the needs of state agencies, and popular knowledge (and beliefs) about India.

pmc-11314059.title: Pain Relief, Functional Recovery, and Chondroprotective Effects of Angelica gigas Nakai in Osteoarthritis Due to Its Anti-Inflammatory Property: An In Vitro and In Vivo Study
pmc-11314059.creator: Hee-Geun Jo, Chae Yun Baek, Yeseul Hwang, Eunhye Baek, Ho Sueb Song, Donghun Lee, Fabrizio Dal Piaz, Giuliana Donadio
pmc-11314059.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Osteoarthritis (OA), characterized by chronic pain and joint degradation, is a progressive joint disease primarily induced by age-related systemic inflammation. Angelica gigas Nakai (AG), a medicinal plant widely used in East Asia, exhibits promising results for such conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the potential of AG as a drug candidate for modulating the multifaceted pathology of OA based on its anti-inflammatory properties.

pmc-11368351.title: Impact of multidisciplinary management via special clinic for the outcome of diabetic foot disease: A prospective observational study
pmc-11368351.creator: Satya P. Meena, Mayank Badkur, Mahendra Lodha, Mahaveer S. Rodha, Ramkaran Chaudhary, Naveen Sharma, Prakash C. Kala, Ravi Gaur, Sumit Bishnoi
pmc-11368351.description: Introduction:Diabetic foot is a common complication of diabetes mellitus, affecting approximately 15–20% of individuals with diabetes. It is a comorbid condition that significantly impacts the routine life of patients. This study aimed to assess multidisciplinary management strategies and their impact on the outcomes of patients with diabetic foot.Methods:A prospective observational study was conducted on 56 patients with diabetic foot.

pmc-12620434.title: A finite element analysis on the execution effects of two novel distalization sequences in clear aligners
pmc-12620434.creator: Hongcheng Xing, Hui Li, Dongliang Zhang
pmc-12620434.description: ObjectiveCurrent clear aligners have the problem of long treatment duration, and the effect of traditional molar distalization sequences is not ideal. To address these issues, this study proposes a new molar distalization sequence. It uses finite element analysis to simulate the long-term movement of teeth, comparing the effectiveness of the new sequence with traditional ones in moving molars backward.

pmc-12717097.title: Private Ownership of Public Trust Wildlife Habitat in Montana, U.S.A. (2004–2023)
pmc-12717097.creator: Alexander L. Metcalf, John W. Chandler, Max H. Birdsong
pmc-12717097.description: Habitat ownership in the U.S. is primarily private, complicating management of public trust wildlife. Under this configuration, the rights and interests of private landowners can be at odds with those of trust beneficiaries. Recent wildlife scholarship has incorporated private landownership into analyses, but limited data accessibility and analysis tools have precluded landscape-wide assessments of landownership patterns and trends.

pmc-13006657.title: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw in an adult with osteogenesis imperfecta: a case report
pmc-13006657.creator: Wang-yong Zhu, Wenjun Wan, Ping-An Wu, Li-wei Zhou
pmc-13006657.description: Bisphosphonates (BPs) are widely used for managing tumor metastasis and bone diseases, associated with a rare complication of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaws (MRONJ). Though reasons are still debated, the MRONJ occurrence in paediatric population suffering osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) and treated with BPs is absent.

pmc-13135238.title: EIF2α–ATF4–CHAC1 Signalling Links ER Stress to Ferroptosis in Human Aortic Smooth Muscle Cells: Mechanistic Insights and Therapeutic Implications
pmc-13135238.creator: Changwen Fang, Xiaolong Du, Yadan Wang, Yiqi Jin, Wenbin Wang
pmc-13135238.description: Ferroptosis—a regulated, iron‐dependent cell death driven by lipid peroxidation—has been implicated in vascular pathology, yet how endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress couples to ferroptotic execution in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) remains unclear. We investigated whether the PERK–EIF2α–ATF4–CHAC1 signalling axis links ER stress to ferroptosis in human aortic SMCs.

pmc-13296023.title: A Synergistic Social Work–Ethnic Education Intervention for Reducing Dropout Risk Among Male Students in Central Guangxi Zhuang Vocational High Schools: A Mixed-Methods and Quasi-Experimental Study
pmc-13296023.creator: Guobin Huang, Lu Hai
pmc-13296023.description: This study evaluated a synergistic intervention integrating school social work and ethnic education for reducing dropout-related risk among male students in Zhuang vocational secondary schools in central Guangxi, China. Using a quasi-experimental mixed-methods design with baseline, post-intervention, and follow-up assessments, 457 students were enrolled and 435 were included in the final analysis.

pmc-13406828.title: Nephron-Sparing Surgery for Unilateral Non-Syndromic Wilms Tumor in a 9-Day-Old Neonate
pmc-13406828.creator: Silvia Ceccanti, Francesco Morini, Loredana Amoroso, Gian Marco Andreoli, Gabriele Masselli, Denis A. Cozzi
pmc-13406828.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Neonatal renal tumors are rare and biologically distinct from those in older children; congenital mesoblastic nephroma is the most common, while Wilms tumor (WT) accounts for about 20% of cases.Neonatal WT usually presents at low stage with favorable histology and excellent outcomes, and radical nephrectomy remains the standard treatment.
